meta.scenario: TeamFlow -- B2B SaaS moving upmarket to enterprise
meta.note: Generated from a real pipeline run (real services, validation gates, provenance edges, framework grounding, persistence, and /why). The LLM boundary is deterministically stubbed, exactly as in the test suite; entity ids are remapped to stable role labels and timestamps are pinned so the artifact is byte-deterministic.

signals.raw_text: Enterprise SSO (SAML) is a hard blocker for the Acme Corp deal worth $240K ARR. Two other enterprise prospects asked for it this month.
Building SAML SSO properly is high-risk: it touches authentication across the whole platform and needs roughly 6 to 8 weeks plus a security review.
Our security team will not approve TeamFlow for company-wide rollout without SSO and SCIM user provisioning.
Admins send 12 to 15 tickets a week asking for directory sync and bulk user provisioning.
Our goal this year is moving upmarket to enterprise, so anything that unblocks enterprise logos should be prioritized this quarter.
We already committed to shipping mobile offline mode this quarter, and the team cannot deliver both SSO and offline well at once.

features.title: Enterprise SSO & SCIM Provisioning
features.jtbd: When I roll out TeamFlow company-wide, I want SAML SSO with directory-synced provisioning, so I can satisfy my security policy
features.description: SAML single sign-on and directory-synced user provisioning for enterprise rollout.

features.title: Mobile Offline Mode
features.jtbd: When I am traveling without connectivity, I want to view and edit tasks offline, so I can stay productive
features.description: View and edit tasks without connectivity, syncing when back online.

parties.summary: Enterprise SSO unblocks the Acme deal and two more prospects.
SSO is a high-risk, ~6-8 week auth change needing a security review.
SSO must be the priority this quarter to unblock enterprise revenue.
The team cannot deliver both SSO and mobile offline well in one quarter.

decisions.title: Build Enterprise SSO & SCIM this quarter, behind a security review
decisions.rationale: A $240K deal and two more enterprise prospects are blocked on SSO, and a customer security team requires SCIM provisioning -- high reach and revenue-gating impact. RICE ranks this highly even at high effort, and Kano classes SSO as a 'must-be' for enterprise buyers. The engineering risk is acknowledged and addressed with a mandatory security review and a phased rollout; the capacity conflict is acknowledged by deferring mobile offline to next quarter.

decisions.title: Defer Mobile Offline Mode to next quarter
decisions.rationale: Valuable but not revenue-gating this quarter; deferred to resolve the capacity conflict with the higher-priority SSO work.

framework_pool.content: RICE scores prioritize by Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort; revenue-gating work with broad reach ranks highly even at high effort.
'Must-be' features such as SSO for enterprise buyers cause disproportionate dissatisfaction when absent; their presence is expected.
